title: How to send a meeting invite in Outlook on Mac: steps for Microsoft 365 in 2026
metaTitle: How to send a meeting invite in Outlook on Mac (2026)
description: How to send a meeting invite in Outlook on Mac: open Calendar, add people, pick a time, then select Send. Fixes for invites that stay unsent.
targetKeyword: how to send a meeting invite in outlook on mac
secondaryKeywords: legacy outlook for mac end of support
intro: Open Calendar, select New Event, give the meeting a title, and add people under Add required people. Then pick a time, add a location or online meeting if you need one, and select Send, not Save.
tldr: Open Calendar, select New Event, and type the people you need under Add required people.
Select Send to deliver the invite. Save only keeps the event on your calendar.
Microsoft lists no keyboard shortcut for a new meeting request. ⌘N opens a new appointment.
Legacy Outlook for Mac stops working with Exchange Online from October 2026. Move to the new app.
If an invite stays saved and unsent, check that you pressed Send, update the app, and test from Outlook on the web.

blocks.text: What you need before you send an invite

You need Outlook for Mac on a supported macOS version. Microsoft's new Outlook for Mac page lists macOS 10.14 Mojave or later and Outlook 16.42 or later on the Current Channel. To check your build, open Outlook and select Outlook > About Outlook. Microsoft lists lower numbers for the Preview channel (16.40) and the Beta channel (16.32), so check the channel as well as the number.

Your account type matters too. Microsoft ties the Scheduling Assistant step to work or school accounts, and its features page lists that tool for version 16.58 and later. A personal account may not show it, so the steps below say where to look for it.

blocks.title: Check the menu names on your screen
blocks.text: Microsoft's Mac page lists two methods without saying which app each one belongs to. The steps in this guide follow the first method and use Microsoft's own button names. If your screen shows a slightly different label, match the closest one and read the tip under each step.
Send a meeting invite, step by step

Work through the steps in order. Each one matches a field or button in the event window. Most invites need only the people, a time, and Send. The other fields are useful, but you can skip them for a quick internal meeting.
Second method: send from the Home tab

Microsoft's Mac page describes a second route that starts from the Home tab. At the bottom of the navigation pane, select Calendar. On the Home tab, select Meeting. Type people in To, then add a Subject and a Location. Select Send to finish. Both routes end at the same Send button, so the same rules about Save apply.
Save or Send decides whether anyone gets it

Save and Send do different jobs. Mixing them up is the most common reason an invite never reaches anyone. Send delivers the invitation to attendees. Save keeps the event on your calendar only. Microsoft's page says that saving an appointment uses Save & Close, which does not notify anyone else.

Microsoft's keyboard list says ⌘ Return sends the open message. That list covers Outlook for Microsoft 365, Outlook 2024, and Outlook 2021 for Mac. It does not name the new app, so test ⌘ Return on a meeting you can cancel before you depend on it.
Add a location, a room, or a Teams link

The location field sits in the same event window as the people fields. Type a room name or an address, and it appears on the invite. Keep it short so people can read it in the calendar grid. Select Add online meeting to attach a video link instead.

Microsoft's features page says Teams is on by default for meetings in the new app, and it lists a Join online meeting button. Give the link a minute before you send. A Microsoft Q&A thread reports that, on version 16.109.2, the Teams join link can take about 3 to 5 minutes to appear. Until then, the meeting shows Online meeting. A moderator confirmed the behavior and offered no fix.

blocks.text: Schedule a meeting in Outlook on Mac with Scheduling Assistant

Scheduling Assistant helps you compare the free and busy times of the people you add. Pick a slot that shows free for everyone who must attend. Then set the start and end date to match. If the slot you want is busy for someone, move the time and check again instead of sending anyway.

Keep the required list short. Every person you add as required is a schedule you need to match. Add only the people who must attend as required, and leave everyone else off until you know they need the invite.
Add someone to a meeting that already exists

Adding a person later has a catch on the Mac. A Microsoft Q&A answer from a community member says the new Outlook for Mac does not offer a choice to send updates only to the added attendee. Adding someone sends an update to all attendees. Outlook on the web and Classic Outlook for Windows do offer that choice.

If that matters for your meeting, you have two options. You can send the new person a separate message with the details, or add them from Outlook on the web. Pick the option that keeps the rest of the group from getting an update they do not need.
Why an invite stays saved and never leaves

A Microsoft Q&A thread reports that in the new Outlook for Mac, the invite saves to the organizer's calendar but is not sent. The poster says attendees were removed when they selected Edit. The poster also says Outlook on the web, legacy Outlook, and the mobile apps work. The only answer in that thread was AI-generated, and no fix is confirmed.
Work through these checks in order. Each one rules out the cause that is easiest to fix.

items: Confirm you pressed Send, not Save.
Open the event again and check that every required person is still listed. If they vanished after Edit, add them back before you send.
Update the app through Help > Check for Updates, then try once more.

Send the same meeting from Outlook on the web. If it arrives there but not from the Mac app, the fault sits in the Mac app. Note the details and report it through Microsoft's community or support channel.

blocks.text: Legacy Outlook for Mac and the October 2026 cutoff

blocks.title: Legacy app cutoff
blocks.text: Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working with Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. If a work account still uses the legacy app, switch to the new app now.

Microsoft's end-of-support page gives the dates. Exchange Web Services retires on October 1, 2026. Legacy Outlook for Mac keeps running on Exchange on premises until October 9, 2029, with security updates only. This guide was researched in November 2026, so the October 2026 date has already passed for work accounts.

Some vendor notices mention a later deadline. Microsoft's own page does not confirm one in the text we opened. Ask your IT admin which date applies to your organization before you plan around any deadline.

To switch, open legacy Outlook for Mac and turn off the Legacy Outlook switch. To go back, open the Help menu and select Revert to Legacy Outlook. Accounts added in one app do not appear in the other, so add your account again in the new app and check your calendars.
Common mistakes that stop an invite from landing

items: Pressing Save when you meant Send. Save keeps the event on your calendar only.
Creating an event with ⌘N and never adding required people. No one gets an invite until you add them.
Sending before you pick the right match from the name suggestions.
Expecting Scheduling Assistant on a personal account. Microsoft ties it to work or school accounts.
Staying on legacy Outlook for Mac with a work account after the October 2026 cutoff.
Trusting a shortcut from a third-party site. ShortcutRef gives ⌘⇧Q for a new meeting request, other sites say ⌘⇧M, and Microsoft confirms neither.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts you can rely on

Microsoft's keyboard list gives five shortcuts that touch this task. ⌘N makes a new appointment in Calendar. ⌘ Return sends the open message. ⌘2 opens the calendar view, ⌘O opens the selected event, and ⌘T shows today. Microsoft lists no shortcut for a new meeting request, so start with ⌘N and then add people.

Some websites list ⌘⇧Q or ⌘⇧M for a new meeting request. Those sources disagree, and Microsoft does not back either one. Open each menu in the menu bar and read the shortcut next to each item. That shows what your copy of Outlook actually uses.
Where to go next

If the meeting needs a shared calendar or mailbox, read [How to add a shared mailbox in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-a-shared-mailbox-in-outlook). If invites fail because the account itself is wrong, check [How to add an email account in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/add-an-email-account-in-outlook). If you are away while invites arrive, [turn on automatic replies](/how-to/turn-on-automatic-replies-in-outlook).

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to send a meeting invite in Outlook on Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft's keyboard list for Outlook for Mac gives ⌘N for a new appointment and ⌘ Return to send an open message. It lists no shortcut for a new meeting request. Some third-party sites say ⌘⇧Q or ⌘⇧M, but those sources disagree and Microsoft confirms neither.

faq.question: What is the difference between Send and Save in an Outlook meeting?
faq.answer: Send delivers the invitation to attendees. Save keeps the event on your calendar only. Microsoft's page says that saving an appointment uses Save & Close, which does not notify anyone else.

faq.question: Why does Outlook show Online meeting instead of a Teams link?
faq.answer: A Microsoft Q&A thread on version 16.109.2 reports that the Teams join link can take about 3 to 5 minutes to appear. Until then the meeting shows Online meeting. Wait a few minutes, then reopen the event.

faq.question: Can I send a meeting invite from a personal Outlook account?
faq.answer: Microsoft ties the Scheduling Assistant step to work or school accounts, so that tool may not appear for a personal account. Microsoft's Mac steps do not cover every personal account feature, so check what your screen shows before you rely on a step.

faq.question: Will everyone get an update if I add someone to a meeting later?
faq.answer: In the new Outlook for Mac, a community answer says adding an attendee sends an update to all attendees. Outlook on the web and Classic Outlook for Windows let you choose to update only the new person.

faq.question: Which Outlook for Mac version do I need for these steps?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists Outlook 16.42 or later on the Current Channel for the new app, on macOS 10.14 Mojave or later. Scheduling Assistant is listed for version 16.58 and later.

faq.question: Does legacy Outlook for Mac still work after October 2026?
faq.answer: Microsoft says legacy Outlook for Mac stops working against Exchange Online mailboxes starting October 2026. On Exchange on premises it keeps running until October 9, 2029, with security updates only. If a work account still uses legacy Outlook, switch to the new app.

task: Send a meeting invite in Outlook on Mac
appliesTo: New Outlook for Mac 16.42 or later on macOS 10.14 or later, with Outlook for Microsoft 365 for Mac
requirements: Outlook for Mac on macOS 10.14 Mojave or later
Outlook 16.42 or later on the Current Channel for the new app
An account that can send meeting invitations
A work or school account for Scheduling Assistant, on Outlook 16.58 or later

steps.name: Open Calendar
steps.text: In the navigation pane, select Calendar. On Microsoft's Mac page, this option sits at the bottom of the navigation pane, so look there first if the sidebar is long.
steps.tip: Microsoft's keyboard list says ⌘2 opens the calendar view. Use the click if the shortcut does nothing.

steps.name: Start a new event
steps.text: Select New Event. This opens an empty event window with fields for the title, people, time, and location. Microsoft lists ⌘N for a new appointment in Calendar, which opens the same kind of window.
steps.tip: An event with nobody added stays an appointment. Add required people to turn it into a meeting invite.

steps.name: Name the meeting
steps.text: Click the title field at the top of the event and type a clear subject. Use the words people will search for later, such as budget review with finance, so the invite is easy to find in a crowded inbox.
steps.tip: Put the purpose first, then the group. Attendees see the subject in their inbox before they open the invite.

steps.name: Add the people you need
steps.text: Click Add required people and type a name or email address. Outlook suggests matches from your contacts as you type. Pick the right match, not the first one, because two people can share a first name.
steps.tip: Microsoft's page names required people here. Add only the people who must attend.

steps.name: Check free time
steps.text: For a work or school account, open the Scheduling Assistant tab. Look for a time when everyone you added shows as free. Microsoft lists Scheduling Assistant for Outlook 16.58 and later.
steps.tip: If a slot is busy for someone, move the time before you send, rather than sending anyway.

steps.name: Set the date and time
steps.text: Pick the start date and time, then the end date and time. Check the day before you send, because a wrong date is the easiest error to miss.
steps.tip: Read the full date line once more, including the day of the week, before you move on.

steps.name: Add a location or online meeting
steps.text: Select Add a location and type a room or address. For a video call, select Add online meeting. Microsoft's features page says Teams is on by default for meetings in the new app.
steps.tip: If the join link says Online meeting for a few minutes, that is a known delay, not a broken event.

steps.name: Set a reminder
steps.text: Choose a reminder so you and the attendees get a heads up before the meeting starts. Microsoft's steps place this choice just before Send.
steps.tip: Pick the reminder for you, and check the attendee settings once you send.

steps.name: Select Send
steps.text: Select Send to deliver the invitation to attendees. Save does not send anything. It keeps the event on your calendar only, so do not select Save and assume the invite went out.
steps.tip: Microsoft lists ⌘ Return for sending an open message, not specifically a meeting, so test it on a meeting you can cancel.

steps.name: Confirm the invite went out
steps.text: Find the event in Calendar and open it. Check that every required person is still listed. If the attendee list is empty after you select Edit, see the troubleshooting list below before you send again.
steps.tip: A Microsoft Q&A thread reports attendees vanishing after Edit in the new app. Treat it as a known report, not a settled bug.

troubleshooting.problem: The invite says saved but never reaches attendees
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm you selected Send, not Save. Update Outlook through Help > Check for Updates and send once more. If it still stalls, send the same meeting from Outlook on the web to see whether that path works.

troubleshooting.problem: Attendees disappear after I select Edit
troubleshooting.fix: A Microsoft Q&A thread reports this in the new app, with no confirmed fix. Add the attendees again, then select Send and check the list. If they vanish again, send this meeting from Outlook on the web.

troubleshooting.problem: The Teams link still shows Online meeting
troubleshooting.fix: Wait a few minutes and reopen the event. A community thread on version 16.109.2 reports a delay of about 3 to 5 minutes, and a moderator confirmed the behavior.
Check that the account is a work or school account. Microsoft lists Scheduling Assistant for Outlook 16.58 and later, so update the app before you check again.
A community answer says the new Outlook for Mac sends updates to all attendees when you add one. Send the new person a separate message, or add them from Outlook on the web, which offers the choice.

troubleshooting.problem: The keyboard shortcut does nothing or does something else
troubleshooting.fix: Microsoft lists no shortcut for a new meeting request, and third-party sites disagree. Open each menu in the menu bar, read the shortcut next to the item, and use that one.
